sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Intermodal ISO Shipping Container Fleet Asset Leasing

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy; unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-jurisdictional corporate distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified legal system influenced by French and German legal tradition; no Islamic Sharia application)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, as in force and applicable to Luxembourg through the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital, as in force and as amended

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital, as in force and as amended
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied, including investment protection provisions
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS MLI), as in force for Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, in particular Articles 101-1 et seq. governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 18 December 2015 on the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 21 December 2017 on the functioning of the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing; applicable EU AML/CFT Directives as transposed into Luxembourg law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft partnership agreement or deed of constitution of the SCSp including all partner identity details and contribution schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary public if the SCSp is constituted by notarial deed; otherwise the foreign notary or counsel certifying the signatures of all partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial act if signed in Luxembourg; if signed abroad, the foreign notary's signature must be authenticated by Hague Apostille, or by consular legalization if the country is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each UBO, general partner, and limited partner holding 25% or more of the partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the issuing state; consular legalization by a Luxembourg embassy or consulate where the issuing state is not a Hague Apostille Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing, certificate of incorporation, or extract from the corporate register for any corporate general partner or corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Domestic company registry or competent company law authority of the corporate partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for states party to the Convention of 5 October 1961; otherwise consular legalization by a Luxembourg diplomatic or consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for each partner's contribution or for the capital to be contributed to the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank and the contributing partner's notary or other qualified certifier
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where required for cross-border evidentiary validity in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney/procuration appointing the Luxembourg resident corporate agent, registered-office service provider, and formation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of the grantor, or a Luxembourg notary where the power is signed before a Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the origin country of the grantor's signature

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification of all general partners, limited partners, directors, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners. Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the US OFAC SDN List, and the Luxembourg national list maintained by the Ministry of Finance and the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified under FATF Recommendation 12 and the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004; PEP status of a partner or UBO, including family members and close associates, triggers enhanced due diligence, written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, senior management approval, and continuous monitoring. Negative-media and adverse reference checks are required. All screening evidence must be retained in the Luxembourg registered office file for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); electronic filing and name search portal at www.lbr.lu and the RCSL gateway through justice.public.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary incorporation filing language is French, with optional German or Luxembourgish annexes. All names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; a non-Latin script name must be fully transliterated into a French-compatible Latin spelling before submission. The SCSp must use either the suffix 'SCSp' or the full words 'société en commandite spéciale' in its statutory name, unless the special law otherwise permits. The name must be distinctive, not misleading as to the legal form, not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity in the RCSL, not contrary to public order, and must not contain restricted terms suggesting a regulated activity without prior ministerial authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCSL rejects a name reservation, the applicant may submit a written reasoned administrative objection to the RCSL within one month of the refusal, including any proposed corrective suffix, transliteration change, or disclaimer. If the objection is dismissed, the applicant may file an annulment application before the Tribunal Administratif within three months of notification of the dismissal under the Luxembourg Code de justice administrative. The statutory name reservation is not extendable as a separate right; upon expiry, a fresh reservation request may be filed, but the original name may be released and made available to third parties in the interim.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a non-regulated SCSp engaged in intermodal ISO container leasing, provided that a Luxembourg registered office is maintained and is accessible for service of process, statutory correspondence, bookkeeping records, and AML/UBO inspection. A virtual or mail-forwarding arrangement is acceptable only when complemented by a substantive commercial agreement with a licensed Luxembourg corporate service provider; a pure letterbox address is not advisable and may be challenged by the tax administration or AML authorities requiring actual decision-making and administrative substance in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is below 2% for a non-regulated container-leasing SCSp with a clean AML profile. The likelihood increases materially if sanctions hits, PEP designation, unexplained source of funds, tax-abuse indicators, or substance-redomiciliation warnings are present; the RCSL, the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit, and the direct tax administration retain legal authority to conduct on-site checks or to demand physical attendance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL name search and name reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) / Luxembourg Business Registers

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Part VII, Articles 944-1 to 944-11, as introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016 creating the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); complemented by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the e-justice regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette, Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: The SCSp charter or partnership agreement (contrat de société / acte constitutif), executed by private deed or by notarial deed where real-property contributions are made, and filed with the RCS through its electronic filing interface or via a notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an SCSp; partners freely determine subscription and payment terms in the charter. Cash contributions are deposited with a Luxembourg credit institution before RCS registration, but no mandatory escrow or blocked-account regime applies. In-kind contributions (e.g., transfer of container fleet assets) must be supported by a fair-value report of an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) annexed to the charter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding limited partner subscribes to one partnership interest in the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) for a capital contribution of EUR 100,000, fully paid in cash to the dedicated partnership account before registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [Registered Office Address], L-XXXX Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name of General Partner] S.à r.l., represented by [Representative], is appointed sole general partner, manager and authorised signatory, together with [Name] as day-to-day manager. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the general partner is authorised to execute and file the charter, RCS Form C, and all ancillary documents for the formation and publication of the SCSp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or corporate law counsel (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg); private deed is sufficient unless a notarial deed is required for in-kind real-property contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the charter containing the corporate name (including the designation 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'), the identity of at least one general partner and one limited partner, the municipality of the registered office, the corporate purpose limited to intermodal ISO container fleet leasing and asset management, the subscription and profit-sharing provisions, and the management and signature powers of the general partner. The charter must be executed in writing by the general partners and by the limited partners. Any contribution in kind must be valued in a report of an approved statutory auditor. The charter should expressly state that the SCSp is a partnership without legal personality and is transparent for Luxembourg income-tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Draft or executed charter (acte constitutif)
Passport or ID copies of all general and limited partners
Certificate of incorporation and RCS extract of any corporate general partner
Statutory auditor's valuation report for in-kind contributions (if applicable)
Tax residence certificates or declarations for all partners
Power of attorney granted to Luxembourg counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the statutory content of the charter, execute a corrective deed or amend the charter and re-submit it within one month; the general partner should promptly remedy any omitted mandatory particulars, such as minimum partner counts or activity restrictions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Luxembourg bank account and deposit of capital contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg licensed credit institution (e.g., Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, BCEE, BGL BNP Paribas, Société Générale Luxembourg) acting under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on anti-money laundering.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed or draft charter to the chosen bank and complete the KYC/KYB procedures. Deposit the fully subscribed cash contributions into a dedicated account opened in the name of the SCSp and obtain the bank attestation required by the RCS filing. The bank will require a beneficial-ownership map of the SCSp, source-of-wealth statements for the limited partner, and an activity description confirming that the container-leasing business does not involve high-risk or regulated trading.
required_dossiers: Executed charter or signed draft for bank pre-approval
KYC/KYB forms for all partners and beneficial owners
Passport copies, residence proofs, and source-of-wealth documentation
Beneficial-owner declaration consistent with the RBE framework
Business plan or activity confirmation letter for ISIC 5229
Completed bank account attestation form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional information on the ultimate beneficial owner or source of funds, provide revised declarations and documentary evidence within the bank's indicated deadline; escalate internally to the bank's compliance committee and, if necessary, select an alternative Luxembourg financial institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), through the official electronic filing portal (e-justice.lu) or by deposit of a notarial deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed charter together with the standardised RCS registration form (Form C for partnerships) through the e-justice electronic filing interface or have the notary deposit the deed. Attach the bank attestation, proof of registered-office address (lease or commercial domiciliation agreement), identity documents, and evidence of payment of the EUR 75 registration duty. The RCS verifies the legal form, name availability, minimum statutory contents, and the appointment of the general partner; upon approval, it allocates the RCS registration number and the Luxembourg identification number (matricule).
required_dossiers: RCS Form C (registration application for partnerships)
Certified copy of the executed charter
Bank attestation of capital deposit
Proof of registered-office address (lease, domiciliation letter or title)
Identity documents of all signatories
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Proof of payment of the EUR 75 registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a suspension or refusal notice, regularise the file by submitting the missing documents or an amended extract within the prescribed deadline; if the requested name is refused due to conflict, promptly reserve up to three alternative names and re-file the amended charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA electronic gazette and filing of the beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice for the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA); Luxembourg Business Registers for the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, cause the standardised publication extract of the SCSp to be published in the RESA, giving the formation erga omnes effect against third parties. Concurrently, file the beneficial-owner declaration with the RBE, identifying any economic owner holding more than 25% of partnership interests or exercising control through profit-sharing rights; the RBE filing is mandatory even when the SCSp is tax transparent.
required_dossiers: Publication extract signed by the general partner
RBE declaration form listing all qualifying beneficial owners
Supporting documents evidencing ownership percentages and control rights
Proof of RCS registration number and matricule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RESA or RBE filings attract administrative fines; file a spontaneous late declaration with a mitigation request and correct any incorrect RBE entry immediately upon discovery; the RCS accepts voluntary remedies with reduced penalties for first-time filers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Assessment of establishment-permit requirement and ancillary tax and social registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale des classes moyennes) via the Guichet.lu portal; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the SCSp maintains a physical commercial establishment in Luxembourg. Pure intermodal ISO container leasing is not a regulated profession, so no sectoral operating licence is mandatory; however, if the SCSp operates a physical depot, warehouse or service office, an autorisation d'établissement must be obtained under the amended Law of 2 September 2011. Independently of licensing, apply for the national tax identification number (matricule) and VAT registration under the AEDT via the standard formalities form; register for VAT where turnover exceeds or will exceed EUR 35,000, and file the CCSS payroll registration for any employees or remunerated managing partners.
required_dossiers: AEDT matricule application (form no. 114)
VAT registration application (form no. C/114 or online equivalent)
Establishment-permit application only when a physical depot or office exists
Proof of professional qualification of the manager (for establishment permit only)
CCSS employee registration forms if personnel are engaged
Certified copy of the RCS extract and charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT queries the registration, provide certified French or German translations of the charter and the RCS extract; if the autorisation d'établissement is refused, lodge an appeal with the Minister of the Economy within 40 days and suspend physical operations pending the ruling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no sectoral industrial operating licence is required in Luxembourg for pure intermodal ISO container leasing activity; if a physical commercial establishment or depot is operated, the Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale des classes moyennes) grants the general establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (asset-leasing SCSp without statutory industrial licence); potential ancillary permit: 'Autorisation d'établissement' for a physical commercial establishment under Luxembourg establishment legislation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report. Container leasing is not listed in Annex I or II of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment. If the SCSp operates an auxiliary container storage, washing or repair depot, a simple environmental declaration or class-based authorisation may be required under the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, depending on the volume and nature of stored materials.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any ancillary site: (i) stormwater and wastewater discharges must meet the quality parameters of the Law of 19 December 2008 on water and the Grand-Ducal regulation of 8 October 2014 transposing EU Directive 91/271/EEC (BOD5 ≤25 mg/L, COD ≤125 mg/L, TSS ≤35 mg/L for urban waste water); (ii) no VOC threshold is triggered for pure storage or leasing, but if painting or coating workshops are opened, compliance with EU Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions and the Grand-Ducal regulation of 10 November 2014 on solvent emissions applies; (iii) all waste streams must be handled by registered collectors under the amended waste-management Law of 21 March 2012, with documented transfer notes and traceability records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance of any container-storage site by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) in accordance with the Grand-Ducal regulation of 28 April 2015 on fire-protection requirements; structural load inspections of stacking racks, lifting equipment and storage yards by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) under the Luxembourg Labour Code (Code du travail); workplace health-and-safety clearance by the ITM before commissioning any depot, including verification of electrical installations and emergency-response plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), 33 rue de la Congrégation, L-1352 Luxembourg; portal: impotsdirects.public.lu. Indirect taxes: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); portals: pfi.public.lu and guichet.public.lu. Business registry and national entity identifier: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), lbr.lu; all administrative filings via MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu to obtain the national identification number (matricule / numéro national); (2) appoint a registered office in Luxembourg and file the partnership deed; (3) for VAT, apply to the AEDT on Form 640 for a 12-digit Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA) before the first taxable transaction; (4) EU-established foreign partners trading through a Luxembourg branch may register directly; non-EU foreign entities carrying out taxable transactions must appoint a VAT fiscal representative (Art. 60(1) VAT Law); (5) as the SCSp is fiscally transparent, income-tax identification is effected through the partners' own domicile filings; (6) register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) only if the SCSp employs personnel. Typical processing time: 2-4 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for Luxembourg income tax purposes (Art. 2 and Art. 4 LIR; Art. 32(1) of the law of 10 August 1915). No corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax is due at entity level; income, gains, and expenses from the container-leasing activity are allocated pro rata to the partners according to their entitlement to profits/losses while retaining their commercial character. Exception: transparency is denied if bearer securities are issued or securities are admitted to trading on a stock exchange (Art. 2(2)(d) LIR). VAT: the SCSp may independently qualify as a taxable person for VAT where it carries out an economic activity in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists. Available elections: (a) Section 182 LIR 'option de taxation' - an SCSp may irrevocably elect to be taxed as a capital company (CIT, municipal business tax, net wealth tax) provided all unlimited partners are Luxembourg-resident, capital is fully paid, a 5-year commitment is made, and no debt securities are listed; request must be filed within 3 months of the end of the fiscal year; (b) hybrid-mismatch alignment elections under Art. 168quater LIR and related provisions implementing ATAD 2 (Law of 20 December 2019, as amended), allowing taxpayers to neutralize deductible/non-deductible asymmetries through a formal election; (c) Art. 64 VAT Law election to waive the small-enterprise VAT exemption and register voluntarily; (d) Art. 63 VAT Law election to form a VAT group (unité TVA) for closely linked entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Established small enterprises: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (Art. 57(1) VAT Law); non-established foreign taxable persons: no threshold, mandatory registration from the first taxable transaction (EUR 0); an SCSp engaged in cross-border container leasing is ineligible for the small-enterprise exemption where its partners are foreign businesses
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping applies. Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing via the PEPPOL 3.0 network for supplies to Luxembourg public authorities and subsidized entities (effective 1 January 2022). B2B invoicing accepts paper, PDF, and structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII) subject to EU authenticity rules (Art. 85-87 VAT Directive). SAF-T reporting is mandatory from 1 January 2024 for VAT-registered businesses with annual turnover above EUR 112,000. Intra-EU recapitulative statements (VIES/EC Sales Lists) and INTRASTAT declarations apply to goods movements above EUR 150,000 (arrivals) and EUR 460,000 (dispatches) annually; container leasing is reported as a B2B service on VIES where the lessee quotes a valid EU VAT number.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Container leasing is a supply of services (leasing of movable property). Zero/outside-scope results are achieved through two routes: (a) B2B place-of-supply rule (Art. 13(1) VAT Law) - where the lessee is an established business, the supply is located at the lessee's establishment: an EU lessee triggers reverse charge in its member state (billing without Luxembourg VAT, citing Art. 21 VAT Law / Art. 196 of the VAT Directive), while a non-EU lessee places the transaction outside Luxembourg VAT entirely; (b) effective use-and-enjoyment relief (Art. 14(1) VAT Law) - leasing of containers used exclusively in international deep-sea traffic or physically used outside the EU, even where the supplier is Luxembourg-established, is outside Luxembourg VAT. Export zero-rating under Art. 155 VAT Law applies only where containers are sold and physically dispatched to a non-EU destination (transfer of ownership, not mere bailment). Substantiation requires a signed lease agreement evidencing international traffic use, a container schedule (box numbers, lease period, destination port), and documentary proof of the lessee's establishment outside the EU (VAT/GST registration, commercial registry extract).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD - Single Administrative Document) bearing the Master Reference Number (MRN) for container sales/exports to non-EU destinations
Bill of Lading (B/L) or multimodal transport document (CMR/AWB) evidencing dispatch from the EU and arrival outside the EU, endorsed to the Luxembourg exporter or its freight forwarder
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer advice evidencing receipt of the invoiced amount (EUR or foreign currency) from the non-EU lessee or buyer
Executed container lease agreement (dry/depot lease) with asset schedule, lease term, destination, and customer's VAT/GST registration number or certificate of non-EU establishment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg imposes no statutory euro-denominated FX repatriation deadline for export earnings; the 180-day benchmark functions as a documentary-reasonableness standard applied by the ACD/AEDT when auditing international service revenue. Where zero-rating is improperly claimed (e.g., EU-established lessee, missing reverse-charge evidence, containers used only within EU inland traffic, or fabricated export documents), the tax authorities retrospectively recharacterize the supply at 16% and impose: (i) late-payment interest on VAT at 0.6% per month (Art. 33 of the VAT enforcement regulation); (ii) late-payment penalties of EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 per taxable period (Art. 92(1)-(3) VAT Law); (iii) false-declaration penalties of EUR 250 to EUR 25,000; and (iv) criminal tax-fraud sanctions under Articles 396-399 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (AO), carrying imprisonment of up to 3 years and/or fines up to EUR 250,000 where fraudulent export documentation is proven. Because the SCSp is transparent, any direct-tax adjustments (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax) flow through to the partners, and the ACD may additionally assess arrears interest at 0.6% per month on underpaid direct taxes, with cross-border exchange of information under the DAC and OECD mutual assistance frameworks supporting recovery from foreign partners.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and payment oversight; no standalone foreign exchange administration authority, as Luxembourg applies complete capital liberalisation within the EU/EEA framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions, as mandated by EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. The euro is fully convertible; there are no exchange control restrictions, no surrender requirements, and no prior authorisation for profit repatriation, dividend distributions, or liquidation proceeds, provided the entity is tax-resident or properly structured and complies with general anti-money laundering, beneficial ownership declaration, and substance requirements. Cross-border payments are unrestricted within the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), and non-SEPA transfers require only standard SWIFT messaging and counterparty bank compliance. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to documentary compliance: tax residence certificate, financial statements evidencing distributable reserves, and corporate authorisations; withholding tax leakage on outbound interest, royalty, or dividend flows may arise under domestic law (15% dividend WHT, 15% interest WHT, 10% royalty WHT) unless reduced by tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary and Interest-Royalty Directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists in Luxembourg. The Grand Duchy abolished all foreign exchange surrender obligations upon adoption of the euro and full capital liberalisation. Exporters must retain trade documentation (invoices, transport documents, customs declarations) solely for VAT, customs, and anti-money laundering audit purposes. There is no requirement to convert export receipts into euro; proceeds may be held in any currency in a Luxembourg or foreign bank account, subject to the entity's treasury policy and OECD/CSSF substance expectations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR and multi-currency); separate Capital Escrow Account for investor contributions

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR); acceptable for low-risk trade settlement and treasury sweep
Operational Account and multi-currency treasury account with dedicated trade finance desk
Operational Account; structured for private-wealth-owned SCSp vehicles
Operational Account; digital onboarding for eligible low-risk corporate structures
Operational Account; strong asset-servicing alignment but conservative AML appetite for pass-through partnerships
Operational Account; local cooperative bank with limited cross-border trade finance capacity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for ancillary operational accounts, LOW as primary treasury bank. Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions supervised by the CSSF can provide SEPA and SWIFT-accessible payment accounts, FX conversion, and virtual IBANs. However, the SCSp's treasury function—container leasing collections from global lessees, disbursements to lessors, and FX hedging—would require a full commercial bank relationship for SWIFT MT103 correspondent coverage, documentary letters of credit, and trade finance instruments. Offshore digital EMIs without a Luxembourg or EU passport are NOT viable for regulated treasury flows because they lack correspondent banking access, may not offer segregated client accounts compliant with CSSF circulars, and create AML/beneficial ownership transparency failures. A hybrid structure of a tier-one Luxembourg commercial bank as primary and an EU-licensed EMI for SEPA collections is acceptable only if the EMI holds funds at a qualifying credit institution and the SCSp maintains full audit trail integrity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Luxembourg SCSp with no statutory minimum capital and a pass-through tax profile, physical attendance of all partners/directors at bank onboarding is generally NOT mandatory under CSSF regulations, but banks retain discretion. In practice, at least one authorised signatory (preferably the general partner's managing director or the corporate administrator) must attend a face-to-face or secure video-identification session with a notarised certificate of incumbency. Remote onboarding is permitted for low-risk structures under Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) using advanced electronic identification; however, banks commonly require: (i) notarised certified copies of the partnership agreement and articles of association; (ii) a certified extract from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); (iii) and a certified copy of the ultimate beneficial owner(s) passport. The general partner (GP), if a corporate entity, must itself complete full KYC. Physical presence becomes practically mandatory if any UBO is a politically exposed person (PEP), if the funding source involves non-EU jurisdictions with high AML risk, or if a bank's internal risk appetite demands personal verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp pass-through classification creates uncertainty over beneficial ownership and management control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the notarised SCSp partnership agreement showing the GP's exclusive management authority; (ii) a CSSF-compliant organisational chart identifying each limited partner and UBO above 25%; (iii) a written confirmation from the registered agent (domiciliation provider) that the SCSp is not a collective investment fund but an operating commercial leasing partnership; (iv) audited or management financial statements proving commercial substance; and (v) a signed AML/CTF policy acknowledging Luxembourg UBO declaration duties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border container leasing flows showing high transaction velocity through tax-favourable jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) master container lease agreements with counterparty names and governing law clauses; (ii) evidence of operational substance: physical office lease, local administrator, fleet management contracts, and bank account in the SCSp's name; (iii) complete transfer pricing documentation supporting arm's-length lease rates; (iv) a rolling 12-month cash flow forecast explaining expected volumes; and (v) copy of tax ruling (if obtained) or tax adviser opinion confirming Luxembourg economic substance and non-abusive structure under ATAD and GAAR.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Investor funding from non-EU jurisdictions with high or enhanced-risk classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble (i) bank and corporate references for each limited partner; (ii) notarised source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements with supporting asset and bank records; (iii) certified passport copies and proof of address; (iv) explanation of the commercial rationale of the Luxembourg SCSp; and (v) confirmation that funds pass through a fully regulated first-tier bank in the investor's jurisdiction before wire transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Conduit or round-tripping concerns because the SCSp has low local fixed asset base and leases only offshore containers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) container fleet purchase invoices, title documents, or lease-in agreements demonstrating the SCSp's real economic exposure; (ii) consolidated fleet asset register with container serial numbers, locations, and lessee utilisation reports; (iii) the SCSp's Luxembourg VAT number and periodic VAT returns; (iv) a detailed substance memorandum covering management decisions taken in Luxembourg; and (v) audited financial statements showing gross lease revenue as the primary income stream.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for investor capital into the SCSp requires: (i) wire transfer from each limited partner's own bank account in the same legal name; (ii) use of SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes corresponding to 'Investment capital' / 'Capital contribution'—for euro-denominated transfers, EBA SEPA payment types may be used but SWIFT with narrative 'LU_SCSP_CAP_CONTRIBUTION_[DATE]' is preferred for audit clarity; (iii) the commercial bank will require a capital call notice issued by the GP referencing the SCSp partnership agreement and the specific investor's commitment schedule; (iv) the bank must verify the UBO profile of the transferring entity and may request ISD (International Swaps and Derivatives Association) or equivalent confirmation if contributions are structured as shareholder loans; (v) incoming funds should be credited to a segregated Capital Escrow Account and only released to the Operational Account upon completion of AML verification and issuance of a partner register entry; (vi) currency conversion of non-euro contributions is executed at standard market rates through the bank's FX desk, and conversion services must not be provided by unregulated counterparties. Non-euro injections must be accompanied by a beneficiary customer due diligence certification and, where applicable, a Loan Agreement or Subscription Agreement, to pre-empt money laundering red flags.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for lease payments to container owners, sub-lessors, and service providers should use the following rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for all non-SEPA or high-value international payments, with proper narrative identifying the underlying invoice (container lease serial, vessel/terminal location, and contract reference); (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for euro payments within the EEA under 100,000 EUR per transaction, with SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) only for operational expenses below 10,000 EUR where the beneficiary bank supports it; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) for large fleet acquisition or lease-in contracts requiring payment against shipping documents—issued by the Luxembourg bank and advised through a second-tier correspondent bank; (iv) Buyer's or Supplier's Credit facilities (avals or standby LCs) if the container leasing arrangement requires guarantees for terminal operators or ocean carriers; and (v) ACH Debit only for recurring service charges within the USA where the SCSp maintains a US-dollar sweeper through its Luxembourg bank's correspondent network. All disbursements must be backed by the invoice matching protocol: to prevent 'phantom invoicing', the treasury function must match the outward wire to purchase orders, delivery confirmations, and container inspection reports, and must maintain an audit trail for VAT reverse-charge or intra-community supply rules under Luxembourg VAT law.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward Contracts (deliverable) up to 12 months tenor, executed with the SCSp's Luxembourg bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a bank's standard FX Master Agreement; USD/EUR and CNY/EUR forwards are permissible for matching lease receipts in USD or renminbi from cross-border lessees.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted Asian or African currencies, where deliverable forwards are unavailable; the SCSp may use NDFs referencing the offshore CNY (CNH) or selected emerging-market currencies solely to hedge contracted lease income streams, provided the counterparty bank is OECD-regulated and the NDF underlying exposure is documented in the lease receivable ledger.

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for converting long-term USD lease liabilities or USD-denominated fleet financing into EUR, or vice versa, on a rolling 1-5 year basis; analogised as interest rate and principal exchange with periodic re-fixing at ISDA fallbacks, permissible only if the counterparty is the primary Luxembourg bank or its investment-grade affiliate.

FX Options (European-style barrier or vanilla) purchased, not written, to protect against adverse USD/EUR and CNH/EUR moves while retaining upside; option premiums are treated as treasury expenses and require board- or GP-approval under the SCSp risk management mandate, with a ban on uncovered option writing.

Currency Futures (listed, exchange-traded) on CME or Eurex for short-dated (up to 6 months) USD/EUR and CNY/USD exposures, executed through a futures commission merchant and margined from the Operational Account; permissible only for transparent price discovery and not for speculative positions.

NDS / FX Swaps with prime counterparties for short-term liquidity hedging of currency mismatches arising from repaying an intercompany loan in one currency while holding lease revenue in another; economic terms documented under a credit support annex, with MTM valuation each month.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS data maintenance and confirmation of registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Rolling anniversary rule; any change in registered particulars must be filed within one month. No fixed calendar-day annual return is imposed on an SCSp.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 under RCS legislation; continued failure may lead to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing and publication (if applicable and unless exempt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (deposited annual accounts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end; exemptions may apply to an SCSp whose unrestricted partners are themselves legal entities or where the partnership qualifies as small.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 5,000; repeated non-compliance may trigger compulsory dissolution ordered by the Luxembourg Commercial Court and registration of the resulting strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO beneficial ownership declaration and register confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after any change in partners, general partner, shareholding percentages, or ultimate beneficial ownership; no separate annual renewal, but RBE verification requests must be answered immediately.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 125 to EUR 5,000 per violation for failure to file or update UBO data; deliberate non-compliance may expose partners or managers to criminal sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a small SCSp. A mandatory audit is triggered when the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three criteria for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total of EUR 4,400,000; net turnover of EUR 8,800,000; average 50 employees during the financial year. Audit is also compulsory if the SCSp is part of a group required to produce consolidated financial statements or if partners holding at least 10% of voting rights so request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2008 on annual accounts and consolidated accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for statutory annual accounts and is mandatory for consolidated accounts of issuers of listed securities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Luxembourg RBE law, the SCSp must maintain current beneficial ownership data. Any change in limited or general partner interests must be declared to the RBE within one month. No separate annual UBO re-filing is imposed, but the RBE may issue risk-based annual confirmation requests, and failure to confirm is treated as an infringement. An internal register of beneficial owners must be maintained at the registered office alongside the other statutory books.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 1,200 – EUR 3,500 (USD 1,300 – USD 3,800) per annum depending on the service provider and Luxembourg location.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 5,000 – EUR 15,000 (USD 5,500 – USD 16,300) per annum when a certified audit is required; nil if the SCSp qualifies for the small-undertaking exemption.

stage_6.entry_description: SCSp name, RCS number (B...), fiscal matricule, registered office and legal form code SCSp.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter full entity details; even if all partners are non-resident, the return must be filed if the SCSp has Luxembourg-source income or a Luxembourg PE.
